subject: Micro-commit uptime exception request — Helix Labs (decision & ops asks)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-08-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Helix ask: 30-day sub-99.95 p95 for search API — ask for exception

Marcus / team,

Helix Labs just raised a formal request in their account call: they want a short-term (30d) "micro-commitment" to a p95 latency floor of <= 95ms for our search endpoint during their peak inference window. They are willing to accept a reduced regional footprint and a temporary credit against monthly usage while we validate the operational approach.

Key points from the customer:
- Window: weekdays 09:00–18:00 PT for 30 days starting 2028-08-22
- Traffic pattern: expected 6k qps bursty, median payload size 128 tokens
- Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 95ms for production route; only for requests routed to quantized-2x model variant
- Compliance ask: they want SOC2 evidence and audit log access for that 30d period

Can you confirm whether product/eng can support this as an exception (runbook / monitoring / fallback) and what the hard blockers would be? I've attached the customer's one-page request (helix_request_v1.pdf).

Thanks — Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Daria Petrov <daria.petrov@helixlabs.ai>
Date: 2028-08-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Helix ask: 30-day sub-99.95 p95 for search API — ask for exception

Thanks Marissa — looping in Karthik for product and Kim for legal/contract signal. Initial thoughts:

- We can potentially hit p95<=95ms for a constrained footprint if we route to a highly-optimized quantized path and reserve burst capacity on Dedicated pools, but it is not free: expected cost uplift ~25–40% during peak periods.
- Operational requirements: dedicated autoscale policy with aggressive pre-warming, strict KV/prefix caching for common queries, and a temporary routing rule that forces requests to a prioritized GPU pool.
- Risk: degradation for non-priority traffic unless we put throttles in place; fallback must degrade to sub-150ms p95 rather than failing.

Questions for product/infra (Karthik):
1) Can the routing layer enforce a temporary policy that pins Helix to a single GPU cluster (us-west-2) for the window without code rollout?
2) What monitoring/tracing minimally required to prove p95 during the window (SLO dashboards + synthetic checks)?
3) Can we ship a 30d DocuSign-first SLA amendment to cover credits and behavioral changes?

I attached the customer's note. If this is feasible operationally, I'll draft an internal brief for leadership.

—Marcus
--
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Helix ask: 30-day sub-99.95 p95 for search API — ask for exception

On Fri, Aug 12, 2028 at 11:05 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — looping in Karthik for product and Kim for legal/contract signal. Initial thoughts:

Short answer: technically feasible with controlled scope. Longer answer and recommended guardrails below.

Operational plan (high level):
- Routing: add a temporary policy that stamps requests with helix_account_id and routes to the `priority_usw2_pool-v2` (reserved capacity). Implementation: config-only change in the routing service, can be live in ~3 business days if quota approved.
- Autoscale: create a pre-warm schedule that keeps X GPUs hot from 08:30–18:30 PT; need a one-off reserved burst bump (estimated 6 extra A100s) — finance/ops will need a signed spend authorization.
- Cache: enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for their top 200 queries (we can onboard these into the cache via a CSV).
- Monitoring: create a dedicated SLO dashboard with 1m sliding-window p95 and synthetic tests at 5-minute cadence; export logs to an access-controlled GCS bucket for Helix.
- Fallback: if p95 > 150ms for two consecutive 10m windows, automatic routing will revert Helix to standard pool and we notify the account.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: model warm-starts underperform for cold-start patterns. Mitigation: recommend a short preload job and a 6-hour soak period before the window starts.
- Risk: operational cost spike. Mitigation: credit formula described below.

Credit model suggestion (for commercial): 20% credit on incremental inference spend above baseline, capped at $40k for the 30d window. This is negotiable but gives finance a bounded exposure.

Next steps I want to validate: quota availability for extra GPUs and quick legal approval for the 30d amendment. If those are green, we can commit to the timeline Marissa suggested.

—Karthik
Product Lead, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Helix ask: 30-day sub-99.95 p95 for search API — ask for exception

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side:
- Helix accepts routing to a single region as a temporary constraint.
- The credit proposal you outlined is acceptable pending a short SLA amendment and our legal sign-off.
- We need DocuSign + a 3-business-day notice before the start date to run an internal release schedule.
- SOC2 evidence request: our security team will need the SOC2 report and a pointer to audit logs for the 30d window. Can you provide an export plan?

Attached is our initial legal redline (SLA-draft-helix.docx). If you can provide an internal decision and an ops runbook by 2028-08-16 EOD PT we can confirm the 2028-08-22 start date.

Best,
Daria

Subject: RE: Helix ask: 30-day sub-99.95 p95 for search API — ask for exception (approval path)

Team — summary and approvals needed:

Decision summary (proposal):
1) Operational: route Helix traffic to `priority_usw2_pool-v2` with a pre-warm of 6 GPUs; enable prefix caching and a 6-hour preload soak. Fallback threshold: p95 >150ms for 2 consecutive 10m windows triggers automatic revert.
2) Commercial: 20% credit on incremental spend above baseline, cap $40k for 30 days.
3) Compliance: provide SOC2 report link + export/retention of service logs to a GCS bucket with access for Helix for the 30d window.

Approvals requested:
- Kimberly: legal sign-off on the DocuSign amendment and confirmation that the credit model is acceptable from a contract perspective.
- Marissa: confirm commercial acceptability and willingness to finalize DocuSign with the customer.
- Karthik: confirm operational feasibility (quota procurement timeline of 3 business days).

If we get yes/green from the three of you by EOD 2028-08-16 we will send DocuSign to Helix and queue the routing change for 2028-08-21 (dry run) — start date 2028-08-22. I'm attaching the two customer docs to this thread for reference.

Thanks,
Marcus
